subject: Egress stewardship and IP handbook for Helix private connector
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@helixhealth.com>
To: jordan_blake@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@helixhealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private connector egress: what we need from Redwood

Hi Jordan / Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this. We're getting ready to onboard Redwood's private connector into our production VPC and need a concise, actionable list of network and firewall requirements so our infra and security teams can scope the change. Key asks from our side:

- Exact IPs or CIDR ranges (if available) and FQDNs to allow for outbound connections from our private endpoint.
- Ports and protocols in-scope (we generally restrict to allowlisted HTTPS-only flows).
- Whether you require DNS resolution to public DNS (or can work with our internal resolver).
- Support for a forward HTTP/TLS proxy (we prefer routing all outbound egress through a central proxy for auditing).
- Any certificate pinning, mTLS, or client-auth requirements that would be broken by TLS-inspecting proxies.
- Guidance on NAT/static egress IPs vs. proxy-based flows for predictable allowlisting.

We also attached our safelist request template (helix_safelist_request.csv). Is there a concise playbook we can give our network ops to implement the minimal set of allow rules?

We need this documented by EOD PDT so the change window on Thursday can be booked.

Appreciate the help — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Cloud Security
Helix Health
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@helixhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector egress: what we need from Redwood

Hi Ben — thanks, good list. Attaching a short playbook and initial draft rules (also copied below) to unblock your ops team. High-level guidance up-front:

1) Preferred pattern (minimal customer exposure)
   - Customer keeps control of egress and uses a static NAT IP (or small CIDR). Redwood's control-plane and runtime accept outbound HTTPS from that IP. This is simplest for allowlisting and avoids TLS inspection issues.
   - Required outbound: HTTPS (443) to our control endpoints, DNS to your resolver, and return traffic on established TCP.

2) Proxy option (audit-heavy shops)
   - Forward proxy works, but two considerations: (a) TLS inspection that re-signs certificates will break our certificate pinning for long-lived tunnels (streaming/WebSocket sessions) and (b) presigned URLs for model artifacts require unmodified TLS. If you must proxy, configure proxy to allow CONNECT pass-through for our hostnames or use mTLS between your proxy and our control-plane (we can provide certs).

3) FQDN vs IP: We can provide short-lived CIDRs on request, but many customers prefer FQDNs since cloud egress IPs may change. If you require absolute static IPs, we can coordinate a static egress range on an enterprise contract.

Quick firewall rules (draft):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.control.redwood-inference.com (SNI: control.redwood-inference.com)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.models.redwood-inference.com (for model fetches)
- Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your internal resolver only
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to storage.redwood-inference.com (presigned artifact URLs)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com only if you opt-in to metrics (we can disable telemetry)

Attachments: helix_safelist_request.csv (filled example), draft-firewall-rules.yaml, nat-design-diagram.png

I'll let Kimberly add notes on mTLS and model artifact mechanics. If you want static IPs, say so and we'll escalate internally.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

On Sun, Aug 9, 2026 at 11:03 AM jordan_blake@redwood.com wrote:
> Quick firewall rules (draft):
> - Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.control.redwood-inference.com (SNI: control.redwood-inference.com)
> - Allow outbound TCP 443 to *.models.redwood-inference.com (for model fetches)
> - Allow DNS (UDP/TCP 53) to your internal resolver only
> - Allow outbound TCP 443 to storage.redwood-inference.com (presigned artifact URLs)
> - Allow outbound TCP 443 to telemetry.redwood-inference.com only if you opt-in to metrics (we can disable telemetry)

Adding some technical clarifications and a small checklist for ops:

- Model fetches and artifact pulls use short-lived presigned HTTPS URLs served from our object storage. These are standard HTTPS GETs and will break if the request body or TLS is modified. Proxy CONNECT passthrough or NATed HTTPS is fine — do not perform TLS termination on these flows unless you are able to present Redwood-trusted certificates.

- Streaming generation uses a long-lived HTTPS/WebSocket session with SNI-based host routing. If your proxy re-signs TLS, we can instead provision an mTLS profile and client cert for your proxy to present to our control-plane (requires CSR -> cert issuance, 1–2 day lead).

- DNS: we recommend resolving our hostnames through your internal DNS so you can route traffic to a transit gateway/proxy. Avoid hardcoding IPs in policies unless you have a static egress range assigned.

- Health checks / keepalives: allow outbound periodic connections on 443 for session keepalive (~1m cadence) to the control-plane. These are low bandwidth.

- If you need strict egress auditing, provide us the proxy IP(s) and we'll advise which hostnames must be exempted from TLS re-signing.

I've attached draft-firewall-rules.yaml with concrete ACL lines your engineers can paste into the edge firewall or transit gateway.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Security Integrations Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@helixhealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: security@helixhealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 14:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector egress: what we need from Redwood

Jordan / Kimberly — this is helpful, a few quick clarifications before we kick the ops change:

1) Do embedding requests and inference (chat/generation) use the same endpoints? Can we consolidate the allowlist to fewer FQDNs?
2) For streaming websocket sessions, are non-standard ports used at all or strictly 443? Our firewall policy forbids non-443 outbound by default.
3) If we choose NAT static IPs, is a single IP sufficient (we expect bursty traffic) or do you recommend a small pool?

If you can answer these, I'll finalize the CSV and raise the change request.

Thanks — Ben
From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@helixhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connector egress: what we need from Redwood

Ben — quick answers and next steps.

1) Endpoints: yes, we consolidate. Primary hostnames to allow: control.redwood-inference.com (control plane + auth), api.redwood-inference.com (generation, embeddings, reranking), models.redwood-inference.com (artifact fetches). We can publish a short FQDN-only allowlist document for ops.

2) Ports: strictly 443. All product traffic uses standard HTTPS and WebSocket over TLS (443). No additional outbound ports required.

3) NAT sizing: a single static egress IP is technically sufficient for connectivity, but we recommend a small pool (2–4 IPs) to avoid throttling and to provide headroom for parallel streams. If you have a single IP NAT today, that will generally work; if you expect large concurrent streams (hundreds), use a pool. We can tune keepalive/backoff on our side if you anticipate bursts.

Next steps / action items:
- Ben: confirm whether you prefer NAT static IP(s) or proxy CONNECT passthrough.
- Ben: upload completed helix_safelist_request.csv into the Drive link and include your change window.
- Jordan/Kimberly: provide final FQDN-only allowlist doc and updated draft-firewall-rules.yaml by 2026-08-10 10:00 PDT.

If you'd like, we can do a 30m runbook walk-through with your infra team tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Jordan
